notes:
- **Make, rename and find folders from the tree.** Right-click a folder for **New folder…**, **Rename…** and **Copy path**. Renaming moves the folder on the disk and takes everything in the catalog with it: ratings, flags, keywords, collections and edits stay on their photographs, and photographs in its trash can still be put back. If the catalog cannot follow, the folder keeps its old name. [Library](https://www.heeler.app/docs/library/).
- **The folder tree from the keyboard.** Tab into the tree and use the arrow keys to move, open and close folders, and Enter to open one. The tree remembers which folders you left open, and the folder you are in stays in view. [Library](https://www.heeler.app/docs/library/).
- **Find and clear missing photographs folder by folder.** A folder holding photographs whose file is gone now shows a missing badge in the tree and the Folders list, and its count leaves them out. Right-click it for **Forget missing photos…**, which removes just those records, and **Flush this folder only…**, which flushes the folder without the folders inside it. Before, a single missing photograph in a tree's top folder could only be cleared by flushing the whole tree. [Library](https://www.heeler.app/docs/library/).
- **One folder, one set of records.** A folder opened once by its own name and again through a link, or typed with different capitals on a Mac or Windows disk, was treated as two folders: each photograph got a second record, and the ratings, keywords and edits on one were out of sight from the other. Opening a folder the catalog already knows by another name now uses the records it has. Photographs that already have two records keep both. On Windows, the tree no longer lists the `$RECYCLE.BIN` and System Volume Information folders at the top of a drive or card, which could not be opened anyway. [Library](https://www.heeler.app/docs/library/).
- **Folders open, and relinks run, without holding up the rest of the library.** Opening a big folder used to keep the catalog busy while it read every file, so ratings, collections and other folders waited behind it; it now reads the files after the catalog is free. Relinking many photographs to a folder looks through that folder once instead of once per photograph, before it touches the catalog, and says how many names it found more than once (it leaves those alone) instead of calling them missing. The list of missing photographs no longer counts photographs on a drive that is not plugged in. [Library](https://www.heeler.app/docs/library/#catalogs-and-missing-files).
- **The folder tree stays the tree you built.** Opening a folder from inside the tree with the folder button now keeps the tree's top folder and opens the branch down to it, and the next launch comes back to that same tree; before, it could start a new tree at that folder, or restore a different one next time. Opening a folder above the tree's top keeps the branches you had open. **Collapse all children** now also stops an **Expand all children** still under way, Expand all children says when it stops at its limit of 200 folders and is offered only for folders in the tree, and a relink no longer takes you back to the folder it started in if you have moved on. [Library](https://www.heeler.app/docs/library/).
- **The right folder lights up.** Two folders in the Folders list with the same name, such as two cards' DCIM folders, both lit up when you were in either, since the list matched folders by name. It now matches by location. And a card or drive opened at its top level now shows the edited badge when photographs under it are edited. [Library](https://www.heeler.app/docs/library/).
- **The folder tree keeps up with the disk.** The tree looked at each folder once, so a folder made, renamed or removed outside Heeler showed up only when you opened its parent. Expanding a row now looks again, and a new **Refresh** item on the folder menu does it on request. Clicking a folder that is gone now says so and takes it out of the tree instead of doing nothing; one Heeler cannot read says so instead of looking empty; and a branch on a card you eject no longer collapses. A folder that is gone but still has photographs in the catalog opens as a list of them, marked missing, ready to relink or remove. [Library](https://www.heeler.app/docs/library/).
- **Flushing a folder keeps track of its trash.** **Flush folder** forgot the photographs in a folder's `.trash` along with the rest, without counting them in its question, and afterwards the trash badge and **Show Trash in system browser** were gone while the files were still in `.trash`. The question now says how many trashed photographs there are, and opening the folder again reads its `.trash` back, with the badge, the way back for each photograph, and its edits. [Library](https://www.heeler.app/docs/library/).
- **A new photograph with a trashed one's name stays new.** If you moved a photograph to the trash and later a different file with the same name arrived in that folder (copying a card again that restarts at IMG_0001, say), opening the folder took the new file for the trashed photograph come back: it showed the old one's rating, flags and edits, and the folder's trash badge disappeared while the original was still in `.trash`. The new file now gets a record of its own, and the trashed photograph stays in the trash with its badge. A photograph you drag back out of `.trash` yourself still comes back as before. [Library](https://www.heeler.app/docs/library/).
- **Hiding or flushing a folder with a collection open.** The collection on screen kept showing photographs from a folder you had just flushed, and clicking off the collection went back to that folder, which added it to the catalog again (or brought a hidden one back). The collection now updates straight away, and clicking off it no longer goes back to a folder that has left the list. [Library](https://www.heeler.app/docs/library/#collections).
- **A photograph whose file is missing can leave the catalog.** **Move to Trash** on a photograph whose file is not where the catalog says had nothing to move: it failed with a message only the Console showed, the dialog closed as if it had worked, and the only way to clear the photograph was to flush its whole folder. On such a photograph the command now reads **Remove from Catalog…** and removes just its record; its edits are kept and nothing on disk is touched. A failed move to the trash is now also shown in the status bar. [Library](https://www.heeler.app/docs/library/#catalogs-and-missing-files).
- **A photograph moved outside Heeler gets its edits back.** If you moved a photograph to another folder outside Heeler and opened that folder before relinking, the photograph showed up there blank, and **Relink** on the old entry failed. Relink now folds the blank entry into the moved photograph, which keeps its ratings, keywords, collections and edits. Flushing a folder also brings a relinked photograph's edits back when the folder is added again, as it always did for the others. And a photograph renamed outside Heeler only in its capitals, or in how its accented letters are stored, keeps its record instead of coming back blank. [Library](https://www.heeler.app/docs/library/#catalogs-and-missing-files).
- **Relinking a folder's worth of photographs finishes the job.** Relinking several missing photographs at once by pointing at a folder stopped at the first one it could not relink, usually because the file it found was already in the library as another photograph. The ones relinked before it had moved, but Heeler went on looking for them in their old places. It now relinks every one it can, leaves the others as they were, and tells you how many found a file that already belongs to another photograph. [Library](https://www.heeler.app/docs/library/).
- **A hidden folder leaves the list.** **Hide folder** said the folder would leave the Folders list, but a folder you had opened stayed on it, and a folder in the tree stayed in the tree. It now leaves both until you open it again with the folder button. Hiding a folder you had only seen in the tree, never opened, now works too, and **Flush folder** on such a folder says there is nothing to flush instead of asking twice and doing nothing. [Library](https://www.heeler.app/docs/library/).
- **A folder opens again after a relinked photograph's old spot fills up.** If you relinked a photograph to where it had moved, and later a file turned up at its old location (moved back, or copied again from the card), the old folder would no longer open. The new file now gets a record of its own, and the relinked photograph keeps its ratings and edits where it is. [Library](https://www.heeler.app/docs/library/).
